proofPassages.supportingExcerpt:
HRD testing assesses evidence about homologous recombination, a form of DNA repair. BRCA1/2 sequencing looks for genetic changes; genomic scar scores measure patterns in tumour DNA; RAD51 foci assays assess a repair-related protein response under defined conditions. These observations are related but are not interchangeable.

A composite genomic instability score can sum loss of heterozygosity (LOH), telomeric allelic imbalance (TAI) and large-scale transitions (LST). LOH alone is one component, not another name for the sum. Mutational Signature 3 is also measured from DNA; it is not a functional protein assay. A genomic pattern does not directly establish that repair is impaired now or guarantee benefit from a PARP inhibitor or platinum. Interpretation depends on the named test, specimen, validated cutoff, cancer and treatment setting.

Telli and colleagues in 2016 used the unweighted sum of LOH, TAI and LST, with a predefined high-score boundary or a qualifying tumour BRCA1/2 alteration, in three platinum-containing neoadjuvant triple-negative breast cancer trials. The score was associated with pathological response. The studies lacked a nonplatinum comparator, so that association does not establish extra benefit from choosing platinum rather than another treatment, or a universal cutoff for PARP inhibitors.

Davies and colleagues in 2017 developed HRDetect from six weighted genomic features, including base-substitution Signature 3, other mutation patterns and a scar index. It was trained on whole-genome sequencing. Its reported sensitivity concerns classification of BRCA1/2 deficiency, not the chance that a patient will respond to a medicine. Performance differed with the cohort and sequencing strategy; the authors called for clinical trials of its predictive capacity.

Cruz and colleagues in 2018 assessed RAD51 nuclear foci in geminin-positive cycling cells and checked DNA damage. In selected germline-BRCA patient-derived xenografts and a small retrospective patient-sample analysis, the foci were a functional surrogate associated with PARP inhibitor resistance. They do not directly show every completed repair event or establish a universal clinical cutoff. Some RAD51-positive, PARP-inhibitor-resistant models still responded to cisplatin, so the two drug-response questions remain separate.
